## Coverage by province

```{r}
#| label: national-map
#| eval: !expr atlas_ready
library(mapgl)
prov <- sf::st_read(file.path(web_dir, "province_metrics.geojson"), quiet = TRUE)
ref <- atlas_summary$reference_threshold
share_col <- paste0("share_within_", ref)
prov$tooltip <- sprintf(
  "<strong>%s</strong><br>%s of people within %g min<br>Median drive %s",
  htmltools::htmlEscape(prov$province), fmt_pct(prov[[share_col]]), ref,
  fmt_min(prov$median_travel_time_min)
)
leg <- atlas_summary$coverage_legend
maplibre(style = carto_style("positron"), bounds = prov) |>
  add_fill_layer(
    id = "provinces",
    source = prov,
    fill_color = list("get", "fill"),
    fill_opacity = 0.9,
    fill_outline_color = "#FFFFFF",
    tooltip = "tooltip",
    hover_options = list(fill_opacity = 1)
  ) |>
  add_legend(
    sprintf("People within %g min of a hospital", ref),
    values = leg$label,
    colors = leg$color,
    type = "categorical",
    position = "bottom-left"
  )
```

## How the atlas works

- **Where people live.** WorldPop 2020 population on a 1 km grid. Each cell is placed at its population-weighted centre, computed from 100 m data.
- **Where hospitals are.** Every OpenStreetMap feature tagged `amenity=hospital` or `healthcare=hospital`, deduplicated and checked.
- **How long the drive takes.** Free-flow car speeds on the OpenStreetMap road network, routed with dodgr to the nearest hospital.
- **Rebuilt every month.** A scheduled workflow pulls the latest OSM extract, recomputes everything and publishes only when automated QA passes.

[Full methodology](methodology.qmd) · [Data quality report](data/data-quality-report.html){target="_blank"}

```{r}
#| label: stamp
#| output: asis
if (atlas_ready) {
  cat(sprintf(
    '<p class="atlas-stamp">Built %s · OpenStreetMap extract md5 %s · WorldPop %s</p>',
    atlas_summary$generated_at, substr(atlas_summary$osm_md5 %||% "unknown", 1, 12), atlas_summary$worldpop_year
  ))
}
```
